title: arxiv_2602.15181v1
universal_lens: The multiview projective geometry establishes a structural isomorphism between synchronized camera manifolds and discrete temporal instances. By treating the dynamic scene as a geometrically constrained neural volume, we derive a unified operator that maps spatiotemporal coordinates to radiance fields without requiring temporally coupled constraints or explicit point cloud initialization. A unified framework for dynamic scene rendering integrates temporal archiving with Gaussian splatting and MLP-based radiance fields, enabling scalable, parallelizable, and robust visual performance analysis.
gsi_mapping: Within GSI, the synchronized multiview setup acts as a high-dimensional prior for Bayesian inference. The neural implicit representation functions as a conformal predictor, mapping historical visual telemetry into compact latent states. This allows probabilistic novel-view synthesis of past events with rigorous uncertainty bounds on rendering fidelity. Bayesian inference maps temporal Gaussian priors to probabilistic scene states; conformal prediction ensures uncertainty quantification for real-time sports analytics.
gse_mapping: For GSE situational reasoning, the time-archival primitive discretizes continuous play into queryable state-transition nodes. The geometrically well-constrained volume rendering translates raw broadcast feeds into persistent spatial graphs, enabling real-time retrospective analysis of player trajectories and tactical formations from arbitrary virtual viewpoints. Situationally grounded state transitions model dynamic motion via time-step MLPs; stochastic control policies enable adaptive replay and predictive motion synthesis.

primitives.name: Multiview Projective Geometry Constraint
primitives.verbatim_quote: To overcome these limitations, we revisit the neural implicit scene representation and propose a neural volume rendering framework grounded in multiview projective geometry.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Neural implicit scene representation: dimensionless latent space; Multiview projective geometry: Euclidean spatial coordinates (meters) mapped via perspective projection matrices.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes a calibrated, synchronized multiview camera network where extrinsic parameters are known and static across the observation window.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails under severe occlusion, uncalibrated ad-hoc camera placements, or highly reflective surfaces violating Lambertian reflectance assumptions inherent to standard volume rendering.

layer2.mapping: Maps the rigid transformations of physical cameras directly to the coordinate inputs of the neural radiance field, bypassing explicit 3D reconstruction.
layer2.telemetry: Photometric consistency error across overlapping camera frustums during training.

primitives.name: Temporal Archival Encoding Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Our method exploits such a default design choice and represents dynamic scenes using synchronized neural representations across multiple camera views, naturally supporting efficient temporal archival and retrospective novel-view synthesis.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Time step t: seconds; Neural representation weights: dimensionless floating-point tensors; Storage footprint: bytes per frame.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes temporal coherence can be captured by independent or weakly coupled neural networks over discrete time steps without massive memory overhead.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when the required archival duration exceeds available compute memory, or when extreme non-rigid deformations violate local smoothness priors.

layer2.mapping: Derives a compact kernel for storing dynamic sports events, replacing raw video streams with lightweight neural weights for infinite-resolution replay.

primitives.name: Geometric Constraint Prior
primitives.verbatim_quote: We argue that a dynamic scene observed under a well-constrained synchronized multiview setup, typical in sports and visual performance scenarios, is already strongly constrained by geometry, and we may not need a temporally coupled constraint or 3d point cloud initialization.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Synchronized multiview setup: N cameras with known poses; Geometric constraint: epipolar geometry limits valid 3D ray intersections.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes the density of camera viewpoints provides sufficient parallax to resolve depth ambiguities purely through spatial intersection.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Degenerates in textureless environments or when all cameras share a common baseline plane, creating depth singularities along the epipolar lines.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's reliance on fixed stadium sensor arrays, proving that dense spatial sampling obviates the need for complex temporal smoothing algorithms.
layer2.telemetry: Reduction in training epochs required to converge compared to unconstrained monocular setups.

primitives.name: Compact Plenoptic Scene Modeling

primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if the spectral bandwidth is too wide for the network to capture chromatic aberrations, or if dynamic range exceeds floating-point precision.

reasoning_traces.think: The fundamental doctrinal shift presented in this chapter window is the rejection of temporally coupled constraints and explicit 3D point cloud initialization in favor of exploiting the inherent geometric rigidity of synchronized multiview setups. Traditional dynamic scene rendering, particularly via 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), relies heavily on high-quality initial point clouds to anchor the optimization process. However, acquiring such priors in live sports or visual performances is computationally prohibitive and often impossible in real-time. The authors posit that the multiview projective geometry itself provides a sufficiently strong prior. By modeling the dynamic scene as a series of rigid transformations across multiple synchronized camera views, the problem transitions from an ill-posed inverse graphics challenge to a well-constrained neural volume rendering task. This approach inherently supports time-archival capabilities, a critical missing feature in existing neural rendering pipelines. Instead of continuously updating a massive 4D representation, the system learns compact neural representations for discrete time steps. This allows for the 'rewinding' of events, synthesizing novel views of past moments with photorealistic fidelity. The mathematical elegance lies in decoupling the temporal evolution from the spatial reconstruction; the spatial geometry is resolved instantaneously via multiview constraints, while the temporal dimension is handled through efficient indexing of neural states. This paradigm directly addresses the bottlenecks of spatial-temporal coherence and memory efficiency, establishing a robust foundation for camera virtualization in high-stakes broadcasting environments.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This methodology traces its lineage back to the foundational principles of Structure from Motion (SfM) and Multi-View Stereo (MVS), which historically relied on explicit feature matching and triangulation. The advent of Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) revolutionized this by replacing explicit geometry with implicit continuous functions. However, NeRF's slow training times necessitated extensions like Instant NGP and 3DGS. The current work retroactively simplifies the dynamic extension of these models by realizing that for controlled environments like sports arenas, the heavy temporal regularization used in methods like D-NeRF or 4DGS is redundant. It returns to the core strength of multiview geometry, augmenting it with modern deep learning capacity rather than complex spatio-temporal splatting mechanics.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From a theory of mind perspective, the system models the opposing agent—the chaotic, high-frequency motion of athletes and balls—as a signal that can be perfectly reconstructed if observed from enough angles simultaneously. The 'mind' of the virtual camera understands that the physical laws governing the scene (rigid body dynamics, conservation of mass) are implicitly encoded in the synchronized pixel streams. It does not need to predict future states (like a coach anticipating a play); instead, it possesses perfect retroactive omniscience. Once the event occurs and is captured by the synchronized array, the neural volume instantly comprehends the entire 3D state, allowing it to answer any counterfactual query about viewpoint or timing without hallucination.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical cross-layer veto must be applied to prevent leakage between temporal frames during the archival phase. If the neural representations for discrete time steps are overly coupled, errors can propagate, causing 'ghosting' or temporal smearing in the rendered replays. Furthermore, we must veto any assumption that this geometric constraint holds for uncontrolled, handheld camera footage; the system strictly requires the synchronized, calibrated nature of professional broadcast rigs. Violating this boundary condition collapses the well-constrained geometry into an ill-posed monocular ambiguity, rendering the time-archival primitive ineffective. Thus, the isomorphism to GSE/GSI strictly applies only within the bounded domain of instrumented sports environments.
